Analyst interpretation

Example of moving beyond dashboard visuals to business decisions.

Billing / Email declined from 88.4% in Jun–Aug 2025 to 63.8% in Jan–Mar 2026. Begin with the high-breach segment, then validate operational hypotheses with owners: routing, staffing, complexity and workload.

Guardrail: observational patterns in generated data are not causal evidence. This example does not claim an intervention will work.

How to test the intervention

Pilot a change in queue routing and triage; measure SLA with consistent definitions, track contact mix and use a suitable control group before attributing any lift.

Evidence to collect: queue backlog, routing decisions, agent capacity, defect rate, contact complexity, weekly SLA and CSAT. Avoid estimating monetary return without validated cost inputs.

03 / Govern the data before trusting the report

The raw-to-curated step includes deliberate defects to test whether a report could reject invalid source rows.

LAND78,072Fictional raw rows
VALIDATE72Rejected exceptions
CURATE78,000Valid interactions
AGGREGATE360KPI mart cohorts

Data-quality rules

25 duplicate identifiers · 20 impossible workload values · 15 missing issue classifications · 12 invalid CSAT values. Invalid rows are quarantined; valid rows feed a single-grain fact table and aggregate reporting layer.

Risk triage proof of concept

Time-ordered train/test split: 36,400 / 15,600 contacts. An interpretable logistic baseline using intake-known variables achieved 0.66 ROC AUC on the synthetic holdout set. The highest-risk fifth had 1.80× the average breach rate. This is educational, not a deployable model; the baseline was trained on the original Jun 2025–Mar 2026 subset, not the five extended months.

04 / Real implementation evidence

Follow the path from stakeholder question to a validated result. The SQL shown below runs against the supplied fictional dataset after importing the curated CSV into a table named contacts.

REQ-04 / Quantify the problematic service queue

Requirement: rank SLA failures, then calculate a consistent cohort rate to assess the proposed pilot.

SELECT COUNT(*) AS contacts,
  SUM(CASE WHEN sla_met=0
    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS breaches,
  ROUND(100.0*AVG(sla_met),1) AS sla_pct
FROM contacts
WHERE team='Billing' AND channel='Email'
  AND month BETWEEN '2026-01' AND '2026-03';
1,827 contacts662 breaches63.8% SLA

05 / Proposed intervention with a decision gate

Business recommendations should be measurable and falsifiable. These pilot thresholds are illustrative proposals requiring stakeholder agreement; no intervention took place.

Controlled trial plan

Weeks 1–2Agree cohort design, KPI definitions, privacy controls and comparison group.
Weeks 3–6Trial targeted routing and ageing-case triage; log exceptions daily.
WeeklyMonitor SLA, queue backlog, FCR and surveyed CSAT versus the comparison group.
Final reviewEvaluate adjusted uplift, sampling adequacy, seasonality and potential adverse impacts.

Decision criteria (proposal)

PROCEED / EXPAND
At least +5 percentage points in adjusted SLA versus a comparable group, with no meaningful deterioration in FCR or CSAT.
STOP / REDESIGN
Declining customer outcomes, unreliable comparisons, unapproved data access, or insufficient evidence.

Risk-model ROC AUC = 0.66 on fictional chronological holdout data: modest discrimination, exploratory only, not a live decision system.
